pr_body:
This PR adds support for storing geo_shape fields as a lucene stored field. The geometry will be stored normalised in Well known binary format (WKB).

Reading geometries from WKB is generally much faster than parsing geometries in WKT or GeoJson in source, therefore we changed the ValueFetcher method to read geometries from the store values whenever are present. This should speed up the fields API. 

In particular we are suing this API in vector tiles so it should speed up this API too. The user has the choice of using more disk space in order to speed up generating vector tiles.

In our test data we saw an increase of ~20% on index size:

```
green  open shapes          Lel6q7CXTfS4xXjl7EB_XA 1 0 13165248 0 6.7gb 6.7gb
green  open shapes_stored   GNko7pi7QQqfx4mexa1YMQ 1 0 13165248 0   9gb   9gb
```

And a ~25% speed up when generating vector tiles:

pr_comment: Hi @iverase, I've created a changelog YAML for you.

review_comment: Nice expansion on the range of tests

I notice we have no error checking here, but perhaps this is not a situation that could ever occur. If we had simply done a cast, we would at least get a class cast exception. This code silently ignores those cases.
I added a an else statement that throws an error
It is broken into two polygons, we store the normalised version of the polygon.
Yes, I understand, the same misunderstanding I made above about it being clockwise.

Should there be more tests in this class? Seems like we have added the most import capabilities to GeoShapeWithDocValuesFieldMapper, so I kind-of expected this test class to test more. Perhaps it is not needed because we have more tests elsewhere?
Yes, and actually this test was wrong. I fixed it and added more tests.
I thought ES handled clockwise only for short edges, but perhaps not?
This polygon is clockwise and ES expects counterclockwise by default, therefore it splits the polygon across the dateline.
Ah, yes, that makes more sense!
Wow! Quite a lot of mocking just to test the `valueFetcher` method. But I guess this was unavoidable.
yep, it is required if we want to mock it,
So I guess the user has no control over whether to pull the stored value or doc values. I assume this is because the stored value is much faster. Are there any negatives to this choice?
The control is wether the user chooses to store the geo_shape or not (default).
